location: Port Ellen, Isle of Islay, PA42 7DU

production.waterSource: Laphroaig's production water comes from the Kilbride Reservoir and Kilbride Stream, flowing across Islay peatland before reaching the distillery.
production.malt: The distillery retains traditional floor malting for part of its barley production. Barley is hand-turned and cold-smoked over locally cut Islay peat; additional malt is sourced externally to complete production needs.
production.stills: Established specialist technical sources document seven steam-heated copper pot stills: three wash stills and four spirit stills. The squat spirit-still geometry and ascending lyne arms preserve a powerful, oily spirit while still allowing meaningful copper contact.
production.peat: Peat is central to Laphroaig's production. The distillery specifically emphasises low-temperature peat smoking using local peat rich in heather, lichen, seaweed and moss.
production.maturation: American-oak ex-bourbon casks are central to the house style, with sherry-seasoned and smaller-format casks used for selected expressions. Maturation takes place at the coastal Islay site as well as within the wider brand's warehousing system.

houseCharacter: Laphroaig builds intensity before distillation through floor-malted barley and low-temperature Islay peat smoking. Its squat pot stills and relatively low-reflux geometry preserve oily, phenolic compounds, while copper contact keeps the spirit from becoming coarse. Ex-bourbon maturation then frames the medicinal, maritime and smoky new make with vanilla and coconut sweetness rather than covering it.
cask23Narrative: Laphroaig's identity begins long before the cask: Kilbride water, floor malting and cold peat smoke establish the famous medicinal and maritime core. The stillhouse is configured to retain weight and phenolic power rather than polish it into a delicate spirit. In the glass, that engineering explains why Laphroaig combines iodine-like smoke and coastal intensity with an underlying sweetness from American oak.
